notes: Status is recomputed by scripts/check_release_readiness.py. Automated gates are re-derived from the repository and are never read from this file.
Evidence expires when a file it declares under 'covers' changes between its recorded commit and HEAD. Evidence with no 'covers' expires on any commit change.

0.1.0a3 was published on 2026-09-06 and verified on PyPI. Its gate evidence is preserved in docs/releases/history/0.1.0a3.md and is deliberately not carried here as satisfied: 0.1.0a4 must re-establish it against its own candidate commit.

RELEASE_PLAN.md states the first 0.1.0a4 gate as one automated gate, "Every 0.1.0a3 gate still satisfied". It is decomposed here into the individual 0.1.0a3 gates, because the checker requires every automated gate to have a real implementation and an aggregate over sibling gates would be circular.
0.1.0a4 is not ready and no gate specific to it is satisfied. Its evidence depends on reference applications built outside this repository, which will be audited separately.

gates.title: Public documentation reflects the implementation
gates.detail: The 0.1.0a3 approval covered the 0.1.0a3 documentation set. A maintainer must review the documentation again against whatever 0.1.0a4 ships, including any composition API the reference applications require.

gates.title: Security and release checks required by QUALITY_GATES.md
gates.detail: The 0.1.0a3 decision recorded experimental-alpha scope on 2026-09-06. Whether that exemption still holds for 0.1.0a4 is a maintainer decision. Threat model, dependency audit, secret scanning and dedicated security static analysis remain unconfigured.

gates.title: Reference applications exist and install Agnara as an ordinary dependency
gates.detail: Applications are being built externally in agnara-project. Note that only agnara is published to PyPI: an application needing HTTP or MCP cannot install an adapter as an ordinary dependency today.

gates.title: No reference application imports Agnara internals
gates.detail: agnara-http declares an empty public surface, so composing HTTP currently requires importing underscore-prefixed modules. This gate cannot pass for an HTTP application until that surface exists.

gates.title: No reference application requires a monkey patch
gates.detail: No evidence can exist until the reference applications being built in agnara-project are complete and audited.

gates.title: Public APIs are sufficient to build the reference applications
gates.detail: A maintainer decides this after the applications are audited. The public API manifest governs only the 41 top-level agnara exports; the subpackage surfaces an application actually imports, including agnara.execution and agnara.core.di, are not yet governed.

gates.title: Dependency injection works naturally from an application
gates.detail: Requires maintainer judgment against real external usage, not repository tests.

gates.title: Capabilities can be declared cleanly from an application
gates.detail: Requires maintainer judgment against real external usage.

gates.title: HTTP exposure works from an application
gates.detail: Blocked on the same missing public composition surface as reference-apps-no-internal-imports. RFC 0006 proposes the model; no implementation exists.

gates.title: MCP exposure works from an application, where applicable
gates.detail: agnara-mcp does declare a public surface, but the distribution is not published, so an external application cannot depend on it normally.

gates.title: Schemas stay coherent across transports
gates.detail: Cross-surface agreement is tested inside this repository. This gate asks for the same evidence from an external application. No evidence can exist until the reference applications being built in agnara-project are complete and audited.

gates.title: CLI and introspection materially help a developer

gates.title: Documentation is sufficient to reproduce the applications

gates.title: Every framework deficiency found by dogfooding is tracked
gates.detail: RELEASE_PLAN.md requires each workaround a reference application needs because of Agnara to be recorded as a framework defect with an Issue, never hidden inside the application.
